To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of electromagnetic field treatment with the special signal protocol used in this study does not produce better results in terms of clinical parameters and the need for subsequent total hip arthroscopy than treatment by minimally invasive curetting and bone grafting alone.

electromagnetic field therapy using Magnetodyn® as an adjunct to minimally invasive curetage and bone grafts for the treatment of osteonecrosis of non-ONF in adults is not superior to curettage alone in terms of clinical outcomes or the need for subsequent total hip arthroscopy.
the clinical parameters of the modified Harris Hip score according to Hadda, Cook and Brinkler, the Merle D`Aubign`e hip score and the VAS were improved after both surgical treatments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and radiographic evaluation of patients with non-ONFH of the femoral neck.
the question of the efficacy of electromagnetic field treatment in non-ONFH.
the question of whether electromagnetic field treatment with the Magnetodyn® system has an additive effect when used in combination with surgical treatment of non ONFH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electromagnetic field treatment with the Magnetodyn® system is not a suitable alternative for the surgical treatment of ONFH.
the electromagnetic field treatment with a special signal protocol, as an adjunctive treatment, is not able to improve clinical results or to prevent total hip arthroprosthesis.

the electromagnetic field treatment with the Magnetodyn® system, using the special signal protocols applied, does not offer better clinical results than curettage and the autologous bone transplantation alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electromagnetic field treatment does not improve clinical parameters or reduce the need for THA in patients with osteonecrosis.
electromagnetic field treatment is not superior to the conventional treatment of non-osteonecrosis in adulthood by curette and bone grafting.
electromagnetic field treatment does not improve the clinical outcome in patients suffering from non-ONFH.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can conclude that the electromagnetic field treatment with magnetodyn, using the special signal program applied in this study, as a supplement to curettage, autologous bone transplantation and bone marrow stimulation in the treatment of non-arthroplasty osteonecrosis of femoral head, does not provide better clinical results and also does not provide better prophylaxis against the need for total hip replacement.
electromagnetic field treatment using a bipolar induction screw (Magnetodyn) does not offer any additional benefits to the treatment of non-ARCO stage 3 and 4 non-ONFH.
the electromagnetic field therapy does not seem to be a useful treatment option for the treatment of non-osteonecrotic femoral head lesions.
